chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Sukri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Juwhari narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ammara narrated to us from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them.

He said: Indeed, Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, was tested without sin, and indeed the Prophets do not sin because they are infallible and pure; they do not sin, nor do they deviate, nor do they commit a sin, small or large.

And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, despite all that he was tested with, did not have a bad smell, nor was his appearance disfigured, nor did any amount of blood or pus come out from him, nor did anyone who saw him find him filthy, nor did anyone who witnessed him feel alienated from him, nor did any part of his body have worms, and thus God, the Exalted, does with all those He tests from among His Prophets and His honored friends,

The people avoided him due to his poverty and weakness in the outward appearance of his condition, because of their ignorance of what he had with his Lord, Exalted is His remembrance, in terms of support and relief.
And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people who suffer the greatest trials are the Prophets, then the next best, then the next best.'

And God, the Exalted, tested him with the great trial that becomes trivial in the eyes of all people, so that they would not attribute lordship to him when they see what God intended to convey to him of great blessings, so that they may deduce from that that the reward from God, Exalted is His remembrance, is of two types: merit and special favor.

And so that they do not belittle the weak for his weakness, nor the poor for his poverty, nor the sick for his illness, and so that they know that He makes ill whom He wills and cures whom He wills, whenever He wills, however He wills, by any means He wills.

And He makes it a lesson for whom He wills, and misery for whom He wills, and happiness for whom He wills. And He is Just in His judgment and Wise in His actions. He does not do to His servants except what is best for them, and there is no power for them except through Him.
ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Ayyub suffer so much if he was sinless?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that Prophet Ayyub’s severe trials were not punitive but a means to preserve his divine lordship (Rububiyyah) from being attributed to his blessings, while demonstrating God’s absolute power over health and status. The narration emphasizes the physical purity of the Prophet during affliction, contrasting it with human ignorance that judged him by his outward poverty and weakness rather than his spiritual station. This serves as a theological lesson on divine justice (Adl) and wisdom (Hikmah), showing that trials are a mechanism for distinguishing true devotion and preventing the belittlement of the afflicted.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-108 Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Askari quoted Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Juwhary, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Am’marat, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB) that his father Al-Baqir (MGB) said,

“Job (MGB) suffered for seven years without having committed any sins. The Prophets (MGB) do not commit any sins, since they are immaculate and pure. They have no deviations. They do not even think of committing any sins whether it be a minor or a major one.

Job (MGB) did not look bad or smell bad even though he suffered from a lot of calamities. He did not even have any puss or bleeding, even as small as the size of the tip of a pen. No one found him filthy and no one was afraid of him (MGB). There were no insects growing anywhere in or on his body. This is how the Honorable the Exalted God treats His dear Prophets (MGB) and noble friends in times of hardship.
The people did not associate with Job (MGB) because he (MGB) was poor and weak and out of their ignorance. They did not know what a great rank he (MGB) had near his Sublime Lord!
The Prophet (MGB) said, “The people who suffer the worst hardships are the Prophets, then those next in rank, then those after them, and so forth.”

The Honorable the Exalted God had Job (MGB) suffer so much that he was belittled in the eyes of the people so that they would not worship him (MGB) when they see the endless blessings of God in his hands. This was done so that the people realize that there are two kinds of rewards and punishments from the Sublime God: One in an especial way as a grant and the second way due to worthiness and servitude.

This was done so that the people never belittle the poor or the ill. This was done so that the people realize that God would make ill anyone whom He wills and treats anyone whom He wills by any means which He wills.

This was done so that it may serve as a lesson to learn from for some people; as a means of destitute and hardship for some other people; and as a means of prosperity for some other people. He is Just in all of his Judgements and Wise in all of his Deeds. He would not do anything to any of His servants unless it was the best thing for them. There is no power save in Him.”
